name: Webinar
description: Reminder / last-call email before a webinar. Single goal: the click to the registration page. Structure: hook visual, promise block, P.A.S. body (problem, agitation, solution), agenda, bonus, three CTAs pointing to the same URL.
goal: Get the reader to click through to the registration page. Do not add links to a blog, a website or social media: every extra link splits the click rate.
rules: One goal only: the click to the registration page.
The three CTAs point to the SAME url; only the wording changes.
Write to one person, not to a list.
Sell the registration, not the webinar. The landing page sells the content.
Benefit over feature: not 'we will talk about X' but 'you will leave with X'.
Keep at least 60% real text: an image-heavy email lands in spam and shows up empty when images are blocked.
Never invent a number for the social proof. No number available means the block gets a factual statement instead.

placeholders.label: Brand name
placeholders.guidance: Used as the logo alt text and in the footer.
placeholders.example: Acme Studio

placeholders.label: Logo URL
placeholders.guidance: 160-200px wide, transparent PNG, hosted on your own domain. Google Drive and Dropbox links break.

placeholders.label: Hook visual URL
placeholders.guidance: 600x338 (16:9). Must announce the topic or the format: speaker's face, screen capture of the method, preview of the bonus. GIF under 1 MB, JPG under 200 KB. A decorative visual that says nothing wastes the reader's attention.

placeholders.label: Hook visual alt text
placeholders.guidance: Describe what the reader will see or learn. Around 40% of opens block images: the alt text must still sell.
placeholders.example: Preview of the 3-step launch method

placeholders.label: Headline
placeholders.guidance: 6 to 12 words creating tension. Pick one angle: urgency ('Last call: tomorrow at 10:30'), curiosity ('What founders still get wrong in 2026'), stakes ('Your list will lose 30% if you do nothing') or outcome ('50 qualified leads in 30 days, without ads'). Ban 'Invitation to our webinar' and 'Don't miss this event': zero tension.
placeholders.example: Last call: tomorrow at 10:30

placeholders.label: Subheadline
placeholders.guidance: One sentence, 12 to 20 words: action verb + measurable result + the constraint lifted ('without', 'in under', 'even if'). A number beats an adjective.
placeholders.example: How to build a full campaign in under an hour, even without a designer.

placeholders.label: Social proof
placeholders.guidance: One verifiable number. By decreasing power: attendees, customers, average rating, a known client name. Without a number, state experience instead ('12 years running these launches'). Never invent it.
placeholders.example: Already followed by 2,600+ marketers

placeholders.label: Cost of entry
placeholders.guidance: Removes the 'how long will this take me' friction before it appears. Be honest, around 200 words per minute.
placeholders.example: (2 min read - 45 min for the webinar)

placeholders.label: Date reminder above the first CTA
placeholders.guidance: Short, scannable, with a coloured anchor. Repeats when it happens to create time scarcity.
placeholders.example: 🟢 LIVE WEBINAR | Tomorrow at 10:30 CET

placeholders.label: CTA 1
placeholders.guidance: 3 to 6 words in the first person, so the reader reads their own commitment. Never 'Click here' or 'Learn more'.
placeholders.example: I'm saving my seat

placeholders.label: Registration URL
placeholders.guidance: The single destination of the three buttons. Add UTM parameters. Any other link in the email splits the click rate.
placeholders.example: https://example.com/webinar?utm_source=mautic&utm_campaign=webinar-reminder

placeholders.label: Problem
placeholders.guidance: One short affirmative sentence describing the reader's reality, no hedging. They must think 'that is exactly my situation'. Never open by talking about yourself.
placeholders.example: In 2026, everything you learned about cold outreach stopped working.

placeholders.label: Agitation
placeholders.guidance: 2 to 3 sentences on the cost of doing nothing: wasted effort, lost time, the widening gap with competitors. Loss aversion moves people about twice as much as the lure of gain, but exaggerated fear triggers rejection. Stay factual.
placeholders.example: You keep sending, and the replies keep drying up. Every week spent on the old playbook is a week your competitors use to book the meetings you wanted.

placeholders.label: Transition
placeholders.guidance: One short pivot sentence that restarts the reading after the negative passage and positions you as the one holding the answer.
placeholders.example: Tomorrow, we fix that together.

placeholders.label: Appointment line
placeholders.guidance: Day + date + time + timezone for international audiences, then the promise. Must be spottable while skimming. Check the date on every reuse: an inconsistent date destroys credibility.
placeholders.example: 📅 Thursday 12 March, 10:30 CET — the outreach system that books 8 meetings a week

placeholders.label: CTA 2
placeholders.guidance: Same URL, a variation of the first label. Placed at the intent peak, right after the promise.
placeholders.example: Save my seat now 🔥

placeholders.label: Agenda bullet 1
placeholders.guidance: Why what the reader does today no longer works. A benefit or a destroyed objection, never a topic. Add a number if you have one.
placeholders.example: Why 80% of outreach sequences now get filtered before they are read

placeholders.label: Agenda bullet 2
placeholders.guidance: What changed, or what the reader does not know yet.
placeholders.example: The inbox rule that changed in January and nobody told you about

placeholders.label: Agenda bullet 3
placeholders.guidance: The concrete method they will leave with, plus the measurable result. Put the most desirable item last.
placeholders.example: The 3-message sequence we use to book 8 meetings a week

placeholders.label: Bonus
placeholders.guidance: Name the asset precisely: template, audit, checklist, script, access. 'The Notion template we use with our 150 clients' beats 'a gift'. Tie it to staying until the end: that lifts the show-up rate, which is the real KPI.
placeholders.example: The outreach template pack, free for everyone who stays to the end

placeholders.label: Bonus proof or scarcity
placeholders.guidance: One line of proof or scarcity to make the bonus credible.
placeholders.example: Already used with more than 150 clients. Not downloadable anywhere else.

placeholders.label: Closing line
placeholders.guidance: One sentence with a TRUE urgency (registrations close tonight, limited seats, no replay). No new argument here, you are closing. A fake scarcity, once spotted, costs you trust for every campaign that follows.
placeholders.example: Registrations close tonight — grab your seat:

placeholders.label: CTA 3
placeholders.guidance: Last variation. This bottom block must work on its own for readers who scrolled straight down.
placeholders.example: I'm taking my seat 🔐

placeholders.label: Postal address
placeholders.guidance: Full postal address. Legally required (GDPR / CAN-SPAM) and checked by Gmail and Outlook.
placeholders.example: Acme Studio, 12 rue de la Paix, 75002 Paris, France
